name: GHRP-2 (Pralmorelin)

lead: GHRP-2 is a lab-made peptide that mimics ghrelin to trigger growth hormone release. Peptide users stack it with GHRH analogues hoping for more muscle, faster recovery, better sleep and sometimes height, and prefer it to GHRP-6 because it tends to cause less hunger.

It binds the ghrelin receptor in the pituitary and hypothalamus, driving growth hormone release through a path separate from GHRH. Human trials show it raises growth hormone and it is used in Japan as a diagnostic test for adult growth hormone deficiency. None cited tested muscle or looks in healthy people, and a 2020 review noted clinical efficacy data for growth hormone secretagogues remain limited.

paras: In peptide communities it is commonly combined with a GHRH analogue such as sermorelin or modified GRF (1-29). Users run it for muscle, recovery and body-composition goals over weeks to months.
It raises appetite, and animal studies show increased appetite and fat mass. Long-term safety data for cosmetic use are lacking, and it is not approved for body-composition use.

angle.text: GHRP-2 is used to raise growth hormone for more muscle, faster recovery, better sleep and sometimes height. It stimulates the ghrelin receptor to release growth hormone, and users like it for causing less hunger than GHRP-6. It is a diagnostic agent in Japan; trials have measured hormone release rather than appearance.

lead: GHRP-2, also called pralmorelin, is a synthetic hexapeptide that prompts the pituitary gland to release growth hormone (GH) by acting on the ghrelin receptor, also known as the growth hormone secretagogue receptor [1][2][3]. Wikipedia describes it as a met-enkephalin analogue and the first drug of its class to be introduced clinically [3]. It grew out of work by Cyril Bowers at Tulane University and by Polygen in Germany on growth-hormone-releasing peptides (GHRPs) [2][4].

The appearance rationale in bodybuilding and peptide communities runs through GH and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1): users report taking GHRP-2, often paired with a GHRH analogue such as sermorelin or modified GRF (1-29), in the hope of better recovery, sleep, leaner body composition and more muscle [5][6][7][8]. Medically, GHRP-2 is marketed in Japan as a single-use diagnostic test for adult GH deficiency [9][10][3]. On looksmax.org it also comes up in height discussions [11].

Human studies show that GHRP-2 raises GH, and that it reliably causes hunger and increased food intake [1][3]. A 2020 review of GH secretagogues in men describes sermorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, ibutamoren and ipamorelin as potent GH and IGF-1 stimulators that can improve body composition, while noting that clinical efficacy data remain limited [12]. Pralmorelin reached phase II trials for GH deficiency and short stature but was not marketed for them, and the World Anti-Doping Agency lists it as prohibited [3].

paras: GHRP-2 is a hexapeptide with the formula C45H55N9O6 and no structural similarity to growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) [1][3]. The GHRP family was built from met-enkephalin analogues containing unnatural D-amino acids; GHRP-6 is described as lacking opioid activity while strongly stimulating GH release [13]. GH secretagogues fall into two classes: GHRH-receptor agonists (GHRH, sermorelin, CJC-1295, modified GRF 1-29, tesamorelin) and ghrelin-receptor agonists, which include the GHRP series, hexarelin, ipamorelin and the oral compound ibutamoren [14].

Many ghrelin-receptor agonists also raise IGF-1, prolactin and cortisol [14]. Ipamorelin is described by Wikipedia as more selective for GH, since it does not stimulate ACTH or cortisol the way GHRP-2 and GHRP-6 do [15].

In Japan GHRP-2 is used as a convenient and safe GH stimulation test for adult GH deficiency, with a peak GH cut-off used to identify severe deficiency [9][10]. Wikipedia says Kaken Pharmaceutical markets it there as a diagnostic agent [3].

Researchers have also tested infusions in prolonged critical illness, sometimes with TRH or GnRH, aiming to reactivate pituitary hormone release and improve metabolic status in patients with muscle wasting [16][17].

Users describe adding GHRP-2 to testosterone-based programs or to training and bulking logs, with sermorelin or modified GRF (1-29) in the same routine, for body composition and recovery [5][7][8][18]. One poster says taking GHRP-2 with a GRF peptide at night seemed to improve sleep quality after a couple of months, and another mentions using it while monitoring IGF-1 [6][8]. Posters on T Nation also describe the combination of GHRH and a GHRP as more effective at releasing GH than either alone [7][19].

GHRP-2 is an agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor in the pituitary and hypothalamus, the receptor for ghrelin [1][20][3]. Wikipedia's ghrelin article says the receptor was characterized in 1999, followed by identification of ghrelin as its natural ligand, and that ghrelin acts on hypothalamic neurons including NPY and AgRP neurons to drive appetite [21]. A 1997 review says GHRPs may counteract somatostatin and partly work through GHRH-mediated mechanisms [1].

Ghrelin-receptor agonists increase body weight and fat mass in animal studies [21]. In mice lacking NPY, GHRP-2 increased fat mass, and in neonatal chicks ghrelin and GHRP-2 reduced food intake [22][23]. Wikipedia notes that GHRP-2 reliably causes hunger and food intake in humans [3]. A 2005 study reported anti-inflammatory effects of GHRP-2 in arthritic rats [24].

Forum posts describe pairing a GHRP with a GHRH analogue so the pituitary receives two signals, and state that the combination releases more GH synergistically [7][19]. Reviews describe GHRPs and GHRH as acting through separate receptors [1]. A 2020 review lists GHRP-2 among agents discussed for body composition in hypogonadal men, where testosterone remains the standard therapy [12].

Human trials have focused on endocrine responses and diagnostics. A 1997 review reports that GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and hexarelin potently stimulate GH release in animals and humans, with mechanisms partly unclear [1][25]. A randomized trial in seven young men reported evidence against a role for the GHRP axis in human slow-wave sleep regulation [26]. A 2007 study evaluated a GHRP-2 test for adult GH deficiency [10].

In critically ill patients, continuous GHRP-2 infusion, particularly with TRH, reactivated pituitary hormone release and produced limited metabolic benefit over several days [16][17]. Wikipedia says pralmorelin reached phase II trials for GH deficiency and short stature but was never marketed for those uses, and suggests a possible reason: its GH-raising effect is lower in people with GH deficiency than in healthy people [3].

A looksmax.org post describes a 2014 Japanese pediatric trial across 84 facilities and 126 prepubertal children with GH deficiency that tested whether GHRP-2 improved growth, and the poster argues from it that the peptide is unlikely to help height [11]. That trial was not independently loaded for this article.
No studies found of GHRP-2 for muscle gain or fat loss in healthy people.

Wikipedia says GHRP-2 reliably causes hunger and increased food intake in humans [3]. Animal studies show increased food intake and fat mass with ghrelin-receptor agonists [22][21]. GHRP-class peptides can raise cortisol and prolactin, according to Wikipedia's secretagogue article, and GHRP-6 users describe heavy eating, which one T Nation poster gave as the reason for choosing GHRP-2 while saying it still disrupted a planned diet [27][14]. A 2020 review notes the lack of long-term efficacy and safety data for GH secretagogues [12].

Elevated GH itself is associated with effects such as joint pain, carpal tunnel symptoms and reduced insulin sensitivity in the therapeutic GH literature, and excess GH over time produces acromegaly [28]. No controlled safety study exists for cosmetic use in healthy people.

GHRP-2 is not approved for body composition or anti-aging use. Wikipedia lists pralmorelin among substances prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency [3], and GHRP-6 and ipamorelin carry the same listing [13][15]. Products sold online as research chemicals are marketed outside any approval pathway [15].

Cyril Bowers, who directed the endocrinology section at Tulane University from 1961 to 2004, led development of the small synthetic GHRPs, and received the Endocrine Society's Monsanto Clinical Investigator Award in 1998 for work on hypothalamic hormones and the GHRP pathway [4]. A 1997 review noted that GHRP-6 was the first hexapeptide extensively studied in humans, with GHRP-1, GHRP-2 and hexarelin synthesized later and available for human study [1]. Wikipedia describes a pituitary and hypothalamic receptor discovered in 1996 and the receptor's natural ligand, ghrelin, identified in 1999 [21]. A 2004 review in Drugs in R&D profiled pralmorelin as an orally active GH-releasing peptide developed by Polygen and Tulane, used as a GH-deficiency diagnostic [2].

On T Nation, GHRP-2 appears in training and weight-gain logs next to testosterone cycles and in pairings with sermorelin or modified GRF (1-29), with some users describing GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and sermorelin as a single peptide routine [5][6][7][19][18]. Another poster says GHRP-6 makes many people eat heavily, which is why they chose GHRP-2 [27].

On looksmax.org, a 2024 thread titled around GHRP-2 being ineffective for height argues from a pediatric trial that the peptide does not add growth, and a reply says a ghrelin-pathway compound is not expected to help [11]. Height discussions on the forum more often name growth hormone itself, IGF-1 analogues and releasing peptides together [11].

lore.intro: GHRP-2 is discussed on T Nation as a GH secretagogue stacked with GHRH analogues, and on looksmax.org in a thread about whether it can influence height [5][6][11].

timeline.event: Cyril Bowers directs endocrinology at Tulane, where GHRPs were developed [4].
The pituitary and hypothalamic receptor for GHRPs is described [21].
A European Journal of Endocrinology review describes GHRP-2 as available for human study [1].
A randomized trial in young men finds evidence against a GHRP role in slow-wave sleep [26]; Bowers receives the Monsanto Clinical Investigator Award [4].
Ghrelin identified as the natural ligand of the GH secretagogue receptor [21]; GHRP-2 and TRH infusion studied in critical illness [16].
Animal studies show GHRP-2 increases fat mass in NPY-deficient mice and lowers food intake in chicks [22][23].
Pralmorelin is profiled in Drugs in R&D as an orally active GH-releasing peptide used as a GH deficiency diagnostic [2].
A study evaluates a simple GHRP-2 diagnostic test in adult GH deficiency [10].
A review examines GH secretagogues including GHRP-2 for body composition in hypogonadal men [12].
